prompt.context: Our client, TastySnack, is a global company with 4 distribution channels. Their stock price is down by 50% and has missed earnings for 3 quarters. They have not been able to focus on growth. They hired Deloitte to answer why TastySnack is unprofitable and what action steps they can take to improve the company's situation.
prompt.question: We have half an hour before meeting the CEO. What info should we ask her for? Then, using the data she provides, perform quantitative analysis to identify why TastySnack is unprofitable and recommend action steps.

clarifying_info.a: Retail, Wholesale, Mass market, and Supermarket.

clarifying_info.q: Has there been any change in market conditions or new entrants?
clarifying_info.a: The interviewer will reveal this through the exhibits when asked.

clarifying_info.q: What geographies does TastySnack operate in?
clarifying_info.a: TastySnack is a global company; the case focuses on overall financials.

exhibits.title: TastySnack Financial Summary 2007-2009
exhibits.shows: Three-year income statement data for TastySnack showing Revenue, COGS, and SG&A for 2007, 2008, and 2009.

exhibits.title: Competitor Financial Benchmarks 2007 vs 2009
exhibits.shows: Revenue for three competitors in 2007 and 2009, plus their 2009 COGS and SG&A figures.

exhibits.title: TastySnack Revenue Breakdown by Market and 3-Year CAGR
exhibits.shows: A pie chart showing TastySnack revenue share by channel and a table of 3-year CAGR and change in price per channel.

exhibits.title: Pricing by Channel: Supermarket vs Mass Market
exhibits.shows: Price to customer and price to end consumer for the Supermarket and Mass market channels.

framework: Revenues: analyze by channel and trend — which segments are growing vs shrinking
Costs: split into COGS (variable) and SG&A (fixed) — track as % of revenue over time
Competitive benchmarking: compare revenue trajectory and cost ratios to competitors
Channel mix analysis: identify whether mix shift is driving revenue decline
Pricing: assess price-to-customer and pass-through to end consumer by channel
Action steps: channel refocus, pricing changes, product/bundle strategy, M&A, management talent

questions.prompt: Analyze TastySnack's top-line and cost trends from Table 1. What is happening?
questions.guidance: Revenue fell 25% from $60M to $45M over two years. COGS fell proportionally (stayed ~50% of revenue), so gross margin is stable. SG&A grew from $8M to $10M (+25%), rising from ~13% to ~22% of revenue. The profitability problem is driven by falling revenues with rising fixed costs, not COGS deterioration.

math.setup: Revenue decline %; COGS as % of revenue; SG&A as % of revenue; operating income 2007 vs 2009.
math.answer: Revenue down 25%; gross margin stable at 50%; SG&A rose from 13% to 22% of revenue, compressing operating margin from ~37% to ~28%.

questions.prompt: Compare TastySnack's performance and cost structure to competitors using Table 2. What stands out?
questions.guidance: All three competitors grew revenues from 2007 to 2009, while TastySnack shrank. This is not an industry-wide decline — it is client-specific. Competitors' COGS and SG&A ratios are broadly similar to TastySnack's 2009 figures, suggesting the cost structure is not uniquely broken. The revenue loss is the core issue. TastySnack is also much larger than any single competitor.

math.setup: Compute COGS% and SG&A% for each competitor in 2009.
steps: TastySnack 2009: COGS 50%, SG&A 22% — SG&A slightly elevated vs peers
math.answer: All competitors are growing; TastySnack's revenue erosion is company-specific. Cost ratios are comparable to peers, but SG&A is slightly elevated.

questions.prompt: Using Table 3, what does TastySnack's channel mix tell you about the revenue decline?
questions.guidance: Mass market is TastySnack's largest channel (45% of revenue) and has a 3-year CAGR of -15% with declining prices (-2%). This is the primary driver of revenue erosion. All other channels have positive CAGRs and rising prices. The company is over-indexed to a structurally declining channel.

math.setup: Estimate mass market revenue in 2007 and approximate decline over 2 years at -15% CAGR.
steps: Decline in mass market alone: ~$7.5M, a major portion of the total $15M revenue drop
math.answer: Mass market (45% of revenue) is shrinking at -15% CAGR; it is the primary driver of TastySnack's revenue decline.

questions.prompt: Using Table 4, compare the margin dynamics of Supermarket vs Mass market channels.
questions.guidance: Supermarket channel margin per unit: $3.72 - $3.35 = $0.37, or ~11%. Mass market channel margin per unit: $3.45 - $3.33 = $0.12, or ~3.6%. Supermarkets are ~3x more profitable per unit AND are growing. This reinforces the case for shifting channel focus toward supermarkets.

math.setup: Channel margin = Price to end consumer minus price to TastySnack's customer.
math.answer: Supermarket earns ~$0.37/unit (~11%); Mass market earns ~$0.12/unit (~3.6%). Supermarkets are ~3x more profitable per unit.

questions.prompt: If TastySnack increases prices by $0.10 for their supermarket customers, what is the incremental revenue impact (assuming unit volume is unchanged)?
questions.guidance: Supermarket is 33% (~1/3) of total 2009 revenues of $45M, so supermarket revenue is approximately $15M. A $0.10 increase on a $3.35 base equals ~3%. Apply 3% to $15M.

math.setup: Supermarket revenue = 33% x $45M. Incremental revenue = (price increase / current price) x supermarket revenue.
math.answer: Incremental revenue from a $0.10 price increase in the supermarket channel is approximately $450K, assuming volume is unchanged.

brainstorming.prompt: What action steps can you recommend to TastySnack's CEO to improve profitability?

categories.name: Channel Strategy
ideas: Determine feasibility of refocusing on supermarket business due to higher margins and positive CAGR
Evaluate reducing exposure to mass market channel where revenue is structurally declining
Assess whether wholesale and retail channels can absorb incremental volume

categories.name: Pricing
ideas: Increase prices in supermarket channel — a $0.10 increase generates ~$450K incremental revenue
Evaluate whether supermarkets can pass the price increase to end consumers
Analyze risks: competitor response, customer price elasticity

categories.name: Product
ideas: Bundle products to increase average transaction size
Introduce new products targeting growing channels (supermarket, retail)
Use loss leaders strategically to gain shelf space in higher-margin channels

categories.name: Competitive Response and M&A
ideas: Consider acquiring a competitor with large supermarket presence to gain channel share quickly
Analyze whether competitors are taking mass market share from TastySnack

categories.name: Cost Management
ideas: Review SG&A structure — it grew 25% while revenues fell 25%; identify areas to reduce
Assess whether economies of scale exist if TastySnack grows through M&A

categories.name: Management and Talent
ideas: Poach successful channel development leaders from competitors with strong supermarket track record
Evaluate whether internal management can execute a channel pivot

recommendation: TastySnack's profitability problem is primarily driven by over-reliance on the mass market channel, which is experiencing a structural decline (-15% CAGR, -2% pricing) and thin unit margins (~3.6%)
Recommend a channel pivot: reallocate investment and sales resources from mass market toward supermarket (positive CAGR, ~11% unit margins) and other growing channels
Implement a modest price increase (~$0.10/unit) in the supermarket channel, estimated to generate ~$450K incremental revenue with limited volume risk
risks: Abrupt de-prioritization of mass market could damage customer relationships
Competitor response to supermarket price increases could erode the gain
Supermarkets may not be able or willing to pass price increases to end consumers
SG&A savings from exiting mass market may not materialize quickly
A channel pivot and potential M&A require capital the company may not have given its weak earnings
next_steps: Deep-dive on mass market economics: at what revenue level does it become unviable?
Model supermarket channel capacity: can TastySnack realistically grow that channel from 33% to 50%+ of revenues?
Commission pricing elasticity study in supermarket channel before implementing price increase
Identify acquisition targets with strong supermarket distribution
Right-size SG&A in the context of a smaller, more focused channel footprint
